messages:
nina: Heads up, reproducible issue in our onboarding sample: coroutine cancel + Retrofit suspend call leaves OkHttp dispatcher threads stuck on older devices (Pixel 2 / Android 8.1). Noticed during device tests.

jorge: Oof. Is this different from the usual auth retry races or the socket interrupt bug?

nina: Feels different. When the coroutine timeout fires we call Call.cancel(), but the call's socket read remains blocked and Dispatcher.queuedCalls count never goes down. After many repeats the test VM runs out of executor threads.

katie: Any chance the Call.timeout() (per-call timeout) isn't being triggered? Retrofit's suspend adapter has some nuance where it delegates cancellation to the Call but doesn't call Call.timeout().cancel() automatically.

nina: Exactly. We're on retrofit 2.9.0 + okhttp 4.9.3. Sample snippet:
```kotlin
// client
val ok = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .connectTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .readTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) // disabled
  .dispatcher(Dispatcher().apply { maxRequests = 64 })
  .build()
// request
withTimeout(1200) {
  api.downloadHugeStream() // suspend Retrofit call
}
```
On cancel we see threads stuck in SocketInputStream.read.

tom: Are you using HTTP/2? I've seen socket interrupt behavior differ between HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 frame reader.

nina: Yes HTTP/2 by default. Forcing Protocol.HTTP_1_1 in the client removes the hang.

jorge: That suggests the Http2Reader thread isn't being interrupted. On older Android kernels an interrupt sometimes doesn't break a native read. OkHttp depends on AsyncTimeout and interrupt bits to wake the read.

katie: Workarounds we should consider for the sample app and onboarding docs: 1) force HTTP/1.1 for device-test builds, 2) set a small readTimeout in CI, or 3) explicitly call connection()?.socket()?.close() inside an EventListener.onCallFailed/onCanceled. Option 3 is hacky but stops thread pile-up in tests.

nina: Tried option 3 in a local patch: close helps but it's racy for pooled connections and can trigger "socket closed" noise in logs.

tom: Also try calling call.timeout().cancel() before call.cancel() when mapping coroutine cancellation to call. That forces OkHttp's AsyncTimeout path. Might reduce the window where native read is stuck.

nina: I tried a patched suspend adapter that calls call.timeout().cancel(); call.cancel() but there was still a small timing window on Android 8.1.

jorge: We should verify on latest OkHttp 5.x snapshots; their HTTP/2 shutdown wiring changed slightly. If 5.x fixes it we can plan an upgrade.

katie: For short-term DX notes, add a section to the Android SDK onboarding: "If your app uses per-request coroutine cancellations on Android <=9, consider forcing HTTP/1.1 or setting a bounded read timeout in CI/device tests." Include a short rationale.

nina: I will open a minimal sample repo and attach a device log + thread dump to the internal issue. The repro is tiny: repeated withTimeout around a suspend streaming call until the dispatcher exhausts.

ci-bot: Device tests failing: device-pool-01 (Android 8.1) 7 failures: dispatcher-thread-exhaustion. See https://ci.internal/4567 for logs.

tom: Thanks, @nina. @eng-runtime can you pick this up? I'll file the internal ticket and link the CI logs & sample.

nina: Filed: INT-4321 with stack traces and a gist of the minimal sample. Will try OkHttp 5 snapshot and report back. :pray:
